prompts.prompt:
You bought a laptop from an electronics shop two weeks ago and it has stopped working. Write a letter to the shop manager.

In your letter,
- explain what is wrong with the laptop
- describe what you have already done to solve the problem
- say what you would like the shop to do

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a laptop that I bought from your Riverside branch on 3 March.

Unfortunately, the laptop stopped working only two weeks after I bought it. The screen goes black a few minutes after I switch it on, and the battery no longer holds a charge. I use the computer for my studies, so this has caused me considerable inconvenience.

I have already tried to resolve the problem myself. I updated the software, charged the device overnight and telephoned your customer service line twice. On both occasions I was promised that a technician would call me back, but nobody has done so.

I would therefore be grateful if you would replace the laptop with a new one or, if that is not possible, give me a full refund. I enclose a copy of the receipt and the warranty.

I look forward to hearing from you within seven days. If I do not receive a reply, I will have to take the matter further.

Yours faithfully,
Karim Mansour

prompts.prompt:
You have seen an advertisement for a part-time job in a bookshop. Write a letter to the manager of the shop.

In your letter,
- say why you are interested in the job
- describe your relevant experience
- explain when you would be available to work

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing in response to your advertisement in last Saturday's newspaper for a part-time sales assistant at your bookshop.

I am very interested in this position because I have loved reading since I was a child, and I would enjoy recommending books to customers. Your shop also has an excellent reputation in the community, and I would be proud to work for it.

Although I have not worked in a bookshop before, I have relevant experience. For the past year, I have worked at weekends in a clothes shop, where I served customers, operated the till and arranged displays. My manager described me as reliable and friendly. I have also organised the library of my university's student society, so I am familiar with cataloguing books.

I am free on weekday evenings and all day on Saturdays and Sundays, and I could start at the beginning of next month.

I would be happy to attend an interview at any time convenient to you, and I can provide references on request.

Yours faithfully,
Laila Hassan

prompts.prompt:
There is no street lighting on the road where you live, and several accidents have happened there. Write a letter to the local council.

In your letter,
- describe the problem
- explain how it affects the people who live in the area
- suggest what the council should do

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to draw your attention to the lack of street lighting on Orchard Road, where I have lived for the past six years.

The road is long and narrow, and after dark it is extremely difficult to see. In the last two months, there have been three accidents, including one in which a cyclist was knocked off his bike by a car that could not see him. Many residents, especially older people and children returning from evening classes, now feel afraid to walk home. Some have stopped going out after dark altogether.

I am convinced that the situation is dangerous and that someone will be seriously injured unless action is taken soon. I would therefore like to suggest that the council install lamps along the whole length of the road, starting with the junction near the primary school, where the risk is greatest. In the meantime, it would be helpful if a temporary speed limit of 20 miles per hour could be introduced.

I would appreciate a reply telling me what steps you intend to take. I would also be glad to meet a council officer to show them the areas of most concern.

Yours faithfully,
Omar Fathy

prompts.prompt:
You are interested in studying English at a language school in another country. Write a letter to the school.

In your letter,
- explain which course you are interested in and why
- ask about the cost and the length of the course
- ask whether the school can help you find accommodation

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to enquire about your English language courses, which I found on your website.

I am particularly interested in your intensive evening course for adults. I have worked as an engineer for five years, and I need to improve my spoken English because my company is expanding into Canada. I would also like to take an international exam at the end of the year, so I would appreciate it if you could tell me whether the course includes preparation for it.

Could you please let me know how much the course costs and how long it lasts? I would also like to know how many students there are in each class, and whether there is a registration fee. If a deposit is required, I would be grateful for details of how to pay it from abroad.

Finally, I am planning to move to your city for the duration of the course. Does the school offer help with finding accommodation, for example with a host family or in a shared flat close to the school?

I would be grateful if you could send me a brochure and an application form. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Hossam Adel

prompts.prompt:
You stayed at a hotel last week and left a jacket in your room. Write a letter to the hotel manager, Mr Hargreave.

In your letter,
- explain when you stayed and where you think you left the jacket
- describe the jacket and say what is in the pockets
- ask the hotel to send it to you and say how you will pay for the delivery

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mr Hargreave,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Mr Hargreave,

I am writing to enquire about a jacket that I believe I left behind at your hotel.

I stayed in Room 214 from 12 to 15 June, and I discovered that my jacket was missing only after I had arrived home. I think I left it hanging on the back of the bedroom door, because I remember taking it off after a long walk on the last evening.

The jacket is dark blue, made of cotton, and the label inside says Harrington. It is a size medium. In the left-hand pocket there is a black leather wallet that contains my driving licence and some personal photographs, and in the right-hand pocket there is a pair of reading glasses in a brown case. These items are of great importance to me.

I would be extremely grateful if you could ask the housekeeping staff to look for it and, if it has been found, send it to my home address. I will gladly pay for the postage; please let me know the cost, and I will transfer the money immediately or pay by credit card over the phone.

Thank you very much for your help.

Yours sincerely,
Mohamed Sherif

prompts.prompt:
The heating in your rented flat has not worked for a week. Write a letter to your landlord, Mr Patel.

In your letter,
- explain what the problem is and how long it has lasted
- say how the problem is affecting you
- ask him to arrange a repair and suggest a convenient time

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mr Patel,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Mr Patel,

I hope you are well. I am writing about the heating in the flat, which has not been working for a week now.

When I turn the radiators on, they stay completely cold, and the boiler makes a loud noise but does not produce any hot water either. I noticed the problem last Tuesday evening and, since then, I have tried restarting the system twice, but without success.

Unfortunately, the weather has become very cold, and the flat is uncomfortable, especially at night. I have a young daughter, and I am worried that she may catch a cold. I have also had to buy a small electric heater, which is expensive to run.

I would be very grateful if you could arrange for an engineer to look at the boiler as soon as possible. I work from home on Wednesdays and Fridays, so either of those days would be convenient, but I could also let someone in on any other day if you tell me in advance.

Please let me know what you decide. Thank you very much for your help with this.

Kind regards,
Nadia Farouk

prompts.prompt:
You would like to attend a training course during working hours. Write a letter to your manager, Ms Roberts.

In your letter,
- describe the course and where it takes place
- explain how it will help you in your job
- suggest how you could make up for the time you will miss

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Ms Roberts,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Ms Roberts,

I hope you are well. I am writing to ask for your permission to attend a short training course next month.

The course is called Advanced Spreadsheets for Business and takes place at the City Training Centre on 14 and 15 October. It runs from 9 am to 4 pm on both days, and it is taught by an experienced accountant.

I believe the course would be very useful for my work. At the moment, I spend several hours each week preparing monthly sales reports, and the course would teach me how to automate many of the calculations. This would save time and reduce the number of mistakes. I could also share what I have learned with other members of the team during a short presentation.

I realise that I would be away from the office for two days, so I would like to suggest a way to make up for the time. I could work two evenings the following week, or come in on Saturday morning, whichever suits you better. I would also make sure that my urgent tasks were finished before I left.

I would be grateful if you could let me know your decision by the end of the week.

Kind regards,
Samir Gamal

prompts.prompt:
Your neighbour, Mrs Walker, has a dog that barks loudly at night. Write a letter to her.

In your letter,
- introduce yourself and explain the problem politely
- say how the noise is affecting you and your family
- suggest what could be done about it

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mrs Walker,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Mrs Walker,

I hope you don't mind my writing to you. I am Sara Ibrahim, and I moved into the flat next to yours in September. I wanted to talk to you about something that has been worrying me, and I thought a letter might be better than a hurried conversation.

For the last two weeks, your dog has been barking loudly between about eleven at night and two in the morning. I am sure you may not have noticed, because you are probably asleep, but the sound comes through the wall of our bedroom. My husband and I have woken up several times each night, and my young son, who has school in the morning, has found it hard to concentrate in class.

I know that dogs bark for many reasons, and I do not wish to cause any trouble. Perhaps your dog is lonely or frightened when it is left alone at night. I wonder if it might help to let him sleep inside your bedroom, or to give him a toy to keep him busy. I would also be happy to speak to you in person if you prefer.

Thank you for understanding, and I hope we can solve this together.

Kind regards,
Sara Ibrahim

prompts.prompt:
Your child's school is organising a trip to a science museum. Write a letter to your child's teacher, Mr Lewis.

In your letter,
- say that you are happy for your child to go
- explain that your child has a health problem and tell him what to do
- ask for further information about the trip

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mr Lewis,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Mr Lewis,

Thank you for your letter about the school trip to the science museum on 20 May. I am pleased to tell you that I am happy for Yara to take part. She has talked about nothing else all week, and I am sure she will learn a great deal.

However, there is something you should know. Yara has a mild allergy to peanuts, and she must avoid any food that contains them, even in small amounts. She carries an emergency injection in her school bag, and I would be grateful if you could make sure that she has it with her during the trip. If she feels unwell, she should be given the injection immediately, and I should be contacted straight away. My mobile number is on the school's contact list.

I would also like to ask for some further details. Could you tell me what time the coach will leave and return, and whether the children should bring their own lunch? It would be helpful to know whether there will be any adults who are trained in first aid.

Thank you very much for your help, and please let me know if you need anything else from me.

Kind regards,
Amira Zaki

prompts.prompt:
You joined a gym three months ago, but you would now like to change your membership. Write a letter to the gym manager, Ms Grant.

In your letter,
- explain which type of membership you have now
- say why you want to change it
- ask what you need to do and whether there will be any extra cost

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Ms Grant,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Ms Grant,

I hope you are well. I am writing to ask whether I could change my gym membership.

Three months ago, I joined the gym on an all-day membership, which allows me to use the equipment and the swimming pool at any time. At the time, I thought that I would visit three or four times a week.

Unfortunately, my working hours have changed, and I now finish at seven in the evening. As a result, I can only come on Saturdays and Sundays, and occasionally on Thursday evenings. I feel that I am paying for a service that I cannot fully use. I understand that you offer a weekend-only membership, and I believe that this would suit me much better.

Could you please let me know what I need to do to make the change? I would also like to know whether there is any extra cost, and whether I would need to sign a new contract or whether I could simply continue with my current one.

I would be very grateful for your advice, as I would like to carry on training at your gym. Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,
Ahmed Tarek

prompts.prompt:
A friend from another country is going to visit your city for a week. Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter,
- say how you feel about the visit
- suggest where your friend could stay and what to bring
- describe some things you could do together

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sam,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Sam,

It was great to get your email! I'm so excited that you're finally coming to visit, and I can't believe it's only a month away.

You're very welcome to stay with me, and my mum would love to meet you. There's a spare bedroom, so you'll have plenty of space. If you'd prefer to be independent, there's also a small hotel round the corner that's quite cheap. As for what to bring, the weather is hot in the daytime, so pack light clothes, sunglasses and a hat. You'll also need a jacket, because the evenings can get cool, and comfortable shoes, since we'll be doing a lot of walking.

We'll have a fantastic time together. I thought we could spend a day exploring the old market and the museums, and another day at the beach, which is about an hour away by train. In the evenings, we could have dinner by the river and listen to live music. If you like adventure, we could even try horse riding in the desert!

Let me know your flight details as soon as you can, and I'll pick you up from the airport.

See you soon,
Hana

prompts.prompt:
You recently stayed with a friend's family for a week. Write a letter to your friend to thank them.

In your letter,
- thank your friend for the visit
- say what you enjoyed most
- invite your friend to visit you

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Chris,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Chris,

I just wanted to say a huge thank you for having me last week. I'm back home now, but I'm still thinking about what a wonderful time I had, and I really appreciate everything you and your family did for me.

Your parents were so kind. I felt completely at home from the very first moment, and your mum's cooking was the best I've ever had! I especially loved the day we spent hiking in the mountains. The views were incredible, and the picnic by the lake was just perfect. I also really enjoyed the evening we played board games with your cousins. I haven't laughed so much for ages, and I'm sorry that I lost so badly!

I'd love to return the favour, so why don't you come and stay with me this summer? The weather is lovely here in July, and I could show you around the city and introduce you to my friends. We could also take a trip to the coast for a few days. My parents would be delighted to meet you as well.

Please say thank you again to your family from me, and let me know what you think about the idea.

Take care,
Mostafa

prompts.prompt:
You have just moved into a new flat. Write a letter to a friend who lives in another city.

In your letter,
- describe the new flat and its location
- explain why you decided to move
- invite your friend to a housewarming party

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Jo,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Jo,

How are you? I'm sorry I haven't written for so long, but I've been really busy packing and moving. The good news is that it's all done at last, and I'm writing to tell you about my new flat!

It's on the fourth floor of an old building in the centre of town, so I have a lovely view of the park. It isn't very big, but it has a bright living room, a small balcony and a kitchen that's much nicer than my old one. The best thing is that the metro station is only five minutes away on foot, so it's easy to get anywhere.

You may be wondering why I moved. Well, my old flat was a long way from my office, and I was spending nearly three hours a day travelling. I also felt that the rent was too high for such a noisy area. Now I'm much closer to work, and I have more free time in the evenings.

I'm having a housewarming party next Saturday evening, and I'd love you to come. You could stay the night, and we could have breakfast on the balcony the next morning. Say you'll come!

Love,
Dalia

prompts.prompt:
You are thinking of buying a new laptop, and a friend knows a lot about computers. Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter,
- say what you need the laptop for
- explain how much you can spend
- ask for advice about which one to buy and where to get it

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Ben,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Ben,

How's everything going? I hope you're enjoying your new job. I'm writing because I need some advice, and I know you're the best person to ask when it comes to computers.

My old laptop is finally dying. It takes ages to start up, and the battery only lasts about twenty minutes, so I've decided to buy a new one. I mainly need it for my studies, which means writing essays, doing online research and joining video calls. I'd also like to watch films on it in the evenings, but I won't be playing any games or editing videos, so I don't need anything too powerful.

I can spend about five hundred dollars, but I'd prefer to pay less if possible. The most important thing for me is that it's light, because I carry it to the library every day, and that the battery lasts for a whole day.

Could you tell me which brands or models you'd recommend? I'm also not sure whether it's cheaper to buy online or in a shop, and whether I should wait for the sales next month. If you're free this weekend, perhaps you could come shopping with me!

Thanks a lot, and write soon,
Youssef

prompts.prompt:
You missed a close friend's birthday party. Write a letter to your friend.

In your letter,
- apologise and explain why you could not come
- say how you felt about missing the party
- suggest a way to celebrate together

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Lily,
prompts.modelAnswer:
Dear Lily,

I'm really sorry that I couldn't come to your birthday party last Saturday. I know how much it meant to you, and I feel terrible about missing it.

The truth is that I woke up that morning with a high temperature and a terrible headache. I thought it would pass, but by the afternoon I could hardly stand up, so my mum took me to the doctor. It turned out to be the flu, and I had to stay in bed for three days. I tried to text you, but my phone's battery died, and I only managed to charge it the next day.

I was so disappointed. I'd bought you a present and was really looking forward to seeing everyone and dancing with you. When I saw the photos on social media, I wished I had been there. I hope you had a fantastic time and that you didn't think I'd forgotten.

To make it up to you, why don't I take you out for dinner next Friday? You can choose the restaurant, and it's my treat. Afterwards, we could go to the cinema if you like. I'll bring your present, of course!

Please forgive me, and let me know if Friday suits you.

Lots of love,
Rana

prompts.prompt:
Some people believe that the best way to improve the performance of employees is to pay them higher salaries.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
It is often argued that higher pay is the most effective way to improve employee performance. While I accept that money matters, I disagree that it is the best solution, because other factors usually have a stronger and longer-lasting effect on motivation.

There is no doubt that salary plays a part. Workers who feel that they are fairly paid are less likely to look for another job, and a pay rise can give a short-term boost to morale. In sales, for example, bonuses linked to results encourage staff to work harder. However, research suggests that this effect fades quickly, because people soon become used to their new income and expect more.

In my view, the quality of the working environment is far more important. Employees who receive regular training, clear feedback and opportunities for promotion tend to feel that their work has a purpose, and they therefore make a greater effort. Similarly, a supportive manager who listens to ideas and recognises achievements can inspire loyalty that no salary could buy. A friend of mine left a well-paid bank job because she felt ignored, and she now works for a smaller company, where she is much more productive and happy, even though she earns less.

Flexible working conditions are also valuable. Many people would prefer to have the freedom to choose their hours or to work from home occasionally rather than earn a little more money. This reduces stress and allows employees to balance their jobs with family life, which in turn improves concentration.

In conclusion, although a reasonable salary is necessary, it is not the most powerful way to improve performance. Employers who invest in training, good management and flexibility are likely to see better and more lasting results.

prompts.prompt:
Children should not be allowed to have their own smartphones until they are at least fourteen years old.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Smartphones have become an essential part of modern life, yet many parents worry about giving them to young children. I largely agree that children should wait until they are around fourteen, although I believe that a basic phone for emergencies could be an exception.

The main reason for my view is the effect on health and development. Young children who spend long hours on screens often sleep badly, take less exercise and find it harder to concentrate at school. Teachers frequently report that pupils who are constantly checking messages have difficulty finishing their homework. By the age of fourteen, young people are generally better able to control their habits and understand the importance of balance.

Another concern is safety. Smartphones give children access to the internet, where they may see violent or inappropriate material, or be contacted by strangers. Social media can also lead to bullying, which is harder to escape when it follows a child home on a screen. Younger children rarely have the maturity to deal with these risks, and even the best parental controls cannot protect them completely.

On the other hand, there are some arguments against a strict age limit. A phone allows parents to contact their children and to know where they are, which is especially valuable when children travel to school alone. In addition, technology skills are increasingly important, and children who never use devices may be at a disadvantage. However, these benefits can be achieved with a simple phone that can only make calls, and with supervised use of a family computer.

In conclusion, I believe that the risks of giving young children smartphones outweigh the benefits. Parents should delay them until adolescence, providing a basic phone if necessary.

prompts.prompt:
University education should be free for everyone who wants to study, and the cost should be paid by the government.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
The cost of higher education is a topic of great debate. Although free university places would bring clear benefits, I only partly agree with this proposal, because I believe that fully free education is not realistic in every country and that support should be targeted.

On the positive side, free education would give every talented student an equal chance. At present, many young people from poor families decide not to apply because they are afraid of debt, even though they might become excellent doctors or engineers. Countries such as Germany, which charges very low fees, have shown that removing financial barriers increases participation and produces skilled graduates who later pay taxes and support the economy. In this sense, the cost to the government is an investment rather than an expense.

However, there are serious practical problems. Universities are expensive to run, and if the government pays for everyone, it must either raise taxes or reduce spending on other essential services, such as hospitals and primary schools. It would also be unfair if taxpayers who never attended university had to pay for the degrees of those who will earn higher salaries. In addition, when education has no cost, some students may not take their courses seriously, and class sizes could grow so large that quality falls.

A more balanced approach would be to provide free places for students with high grades or low family incomes, and to offer loans that are repaid only when graduates earn a reasonable salary. This keeps education accessible without placing an impossible burden on public budgets.

In conclusion, I agree that no one should be prevented from studying by lack of money, but I do not think that making all university education free is the best way to achieve this.

prompts.prompt:
Protecting the environment is the responsibility of governments, not individuals.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Environmental problems such as pollution and climate change affect everyone. Some people claim that only governments can solve them, but I disagree to a large extent. I believe that governments and individuals both have important roles, and that neither can succeed without the other.

It is true that governments have powers that individuals lack. They can pass laws that limit factory emissions, ban the most harmful chemicals and invest in public transport and renewable energy. A single citizen cannot build a wind farm or force a company to clean the water it releases into a river. When governments act, the results are large and fast. For instance, in many countries, a small charge on plastic bags led to an immediate and dramatic reduction in their use.

However, laws alone are not enough, because they depend on the cooperation of ordinary people. If households continue to waste energy and throw rubbish on the street, even the best policies will fail. Individual choices also send a message to businesses: when consumers prefer products with less packaging or buy locally grown food, companies change their behaviour to match. Moreover, citizens who are concerned about the environment vote for politicians who take it seriously, so personal attitudes shape government decisions.

In my own city, a campaign by residents to separate their waste for recycling convinced the municipality to build a modern recycling plant. This shows how people and governments can reinforce each other.

In conclusion, protecting the environment is a shared responsibility. Governments must provide the laws and infrastructure, but individuals must change their daily habits and press for change. Placing the whole burden on governments ignores the power that ordinary people have.

prompts.prompt:
Some people prefer to live in a large city. Others think that life in a small town or the countryside is better.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
The question of where to live divides opinion. Some people are attracted by the energy and opportunities of big cities, while others prefer the calm of small towns. Both views have merit, but I personally find the advantages of a smaller place more convincing.

Those who favour cities usually point to jobs and services. Large cities offer a wider range of careers, higher salaries and better chances to meet people from different backgrounds. They also have excellent hospitals, universities and public transport, as well as a rich cultural life, with theatres, museums and restaurants from all over the world. For young professionals in particular, this variety can be exciting and helpful in building a career.

On the other hand, supporters of small-town life emphasise quality of life. Housing is much cheaper, so families can afford more space, and commuting takes minutes rather than hours. There is less noise, traffic and air pollution, which is better for health, and neighbours often know and support one another. Children can play outside safely, and the pace of life is more relaxed. I have a cousin who moved from the capital to a town of fifty thousand people, and she says that she now has more time for her family and spends less on rent.

In my opinion, the best choice depends on a person's stage of life. Young people may benefit from the opportunities of a big city, but I believe that, when raising a family, a smaller community provides a healthier and more balanced environment. Furthermore, the growth of remote working means that jobs are no longer concentrated in cities.

In conclusion, while cities offer excitement and career prospects, I think that small towns provide a better overall quality of life for most people.

prompts.prompt:
Some people believe that governments should spend more money on preventing illness by encouraging healthy lifestyles. Others think that more money should be spent on treating people who are already ill.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Health budgets are always limited, and governments must decide how to divide them. Some argue that prevention should be the priority, while others believe that treating patients is more urgent. In my opinion, both are necessary, but prevention deserves more investment than it receives.

Those who support spending on treatment have a strong moral argument. People who are suffering from serious conditions such as cancer or heart disease need immediate care, and a society that fails to provide it is neglecting its basic duty. Hospitals also need modern equipment and well-trained staff, and delays in treatment can cost lives. For these critics, it seems unfair to spend public money on advertising campaigns when patients are waiting months for operations.

However, prevention can be more effective in the long term. Many of the most common illnesses, including diabetes and lung disease, are closely connected to diet, smoking and lack of exercise. If governments promote healthy eating in schools, build cycle lanes and tax tobacco and sugary drinks, fewer people will become ill in the first place. This reduces pressure on hospitals and saves large sums of money. For example, anti-smoking laws in several countries have been followed by a significant fall in heart attacks.

I believe that the most sensible policy is a balanced one, but with a stronger emphasis on prevention than at present. Treatment will always be needed, because not all illness can be avoided, and it would be wrong to reduce it. Yet a small increase in spending on education and public health can prevent far greater costs later.

In conclusion, although treating the sick is essential, preventing illness is wiser and cheaper, and governments should give it greater priority.

prompts.prompt:
Some people think that young children are best looked after at home by their parents. Others believe that it is better for children to attend nursery or pre-school from an early age.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Parents face a difficult choice when their children are very young. Some feel that the home is the best place for early childhood, while others prefer nurseries. Both options have strengths, and I believe that the best solution is a mixture of the two.

Supporters of home care argue that young children need the security and attention that only their parents can provide. A child who stays with the family develops a strong emotional bond and receives individual care, which can build confidence. Parents can also pass on their own values and language. In addition, young children who spend long days in a group are more likely to catch infections, and some feel anxious when they are separated from their mothers.

On the other hand, nurseries bring benefits that are difficult to achieve at home. Trained staff organise activities that develop language, numbers and creativity, and children learn to share, take turns and make friends. This social experience helps them to adapt more easily when they start primary school. Nurseries are also essential for families in which both parents must work, and they allow many women to continue their careers. A neighbour of mine sent her daughter to nursery from the age of two, and the girl could read simple words before her first day at school.

In my view, the choice should depend on the child and the family. Very young babies are probably better cared for at home, but from about the age of three, a few hours each day with other children is valuable. Part-time attendance can combine the advantages of both approaches.

In conclusion, neither option is perfect for every family, and I believe that a combination of loving care at home and some experience in pre-school offers children the best start in life.

prompts.prompt:
Some people believe that it is better to work in your own country. Others think that people should move abroad to find better jobs.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
In an age of global communication, many professionals have the choice of building a career at home or overseas. Some people believe that staying in their own country is wiser, while others see greater opportunities abroad. Each option has advantages, but I think that working abroad, at least for a period, can be very rewarding.

Those who prefer to stay at home usually mention family and culture. Living near relatives provides emotional support, and parents who are ageing can be cared for by their children. Moreover, workers in their own country understand the language, laws and customs, so they avoid the stress of adjusting to a different way of life. Moving abroad can also be expensive and uncertain, because it may be difficult to have qualifications recognised or to find a stable job at the start.

However, there are strong reasons for going abroad. In some countries, salaries and working conditions are much better, especially in fields such as medicine, engineering and information technology. This allows people to save money and support their families, even from a distance. Working in another country also provides valuable experience: employees learn new skills, meet colleagues from many cultures and improve their language ability, all of which makes them more attractive to employers. One of my colleagues spent three years working in Canada and later returned home to a much better position.

In my opinion, it is a personal decision that depends on circumstances. For young, ambitious people without family commitments, a period abroad can accelerate their careers. Later, many of them return and use their experience to benefit their own community.

In conclusion, working in one's own country offers security and closeness to family, but working abroad provides opportunities for growth, and I believe that these often justify the challenges involved.

prompts.prompt:
More and more people are buying goods online instead of going to shops.

Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Online shopping has grown rapidly over the last decade, and many people now buy everything from clothes to food on their phones. Although this trend has certain drawbacks, I believe that the advantages outweigh them.

The greatest benefit is convenience. Shoppers can compare prices and read reviews from home at any time of day, which saves both time and money. For people who live in remote areas, have disabilities or care for young children, being able to order products without travelling is extremely valuable. Online stores also offer a much wider choice than any physical shop, and special products can be delivered from other countries. In addition, competition between websites often leads to lower prices and generous discounts.

Nevertheless, there are real disadvantages. One is the damage to local businesses. When customers switch to large internet companies, small shops lose income and may close, which reduces jobs and makes town centres less lively. Another is that buyers cannot see or try on items before they pay, so they may receive goods that are the wrong size or poor quality and have to go through the trouble of returning them. There are also environmental concerns, since delivery vans and excess packaging add to pollution, and security risks, as personal data can be stolen.

However, many of these problems can be reduced. Local shops can sell online themselves, and clear return policies protect customers. Delivery companies are increasingly using electric vehicles and recyclable packaging. Meanwhile, the personal and economic benefits of shopping online are enormous and continue to grow.

In conclusion, despite the harm to traditional shops and some environmental and security issues, I believe that the convenience, choice and savings of online shopping make it a mainly positive development.

prompts.prompt:
An increasing number of students choose to study at universities in other countries.

Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Studying abroad has become much more common as travel and communication have improved. This trend has some disadvantages, but in my opinion the advantages are greater, especially for the individual student.

First, a foreign university can offer a higher standard of education than is available at home. Students may gain access to modern laboratories, famous professors and subjects that are not taught in their own country. They also improve their language skills quickly, because they use the language every day in class and in daily life. In addition, a degree from an overseas university is often respected by employers, which can lead to better job prospects. Beyond academic benefits, living abroad teaches independence and tolerance, as students learn to manage money, solve problems alone and work with people from different cultures.

On the other hand, there are disadvantages. The cost is considerable, since international students usually pay higher fees and must also cover accommodation and travel. Many young people feel lonely and homesick, particularly in the first months, and some find it hard to adapt to unfamiliar food and weather. There is also the problem of the so-called brain drain: if the most talented students settle in the country where they studied, their home country loses the skills it needs.

Nevertheless, many students return with valuable knowledge and international contacts, and governments can encourage this by offering attractive jobs. Scholarships and exchange programmes can also reduce the financial burden for families, and universities now provide support for foreign students to help them feel welcome.

In conclusion, although studying abroad is costly and can be difficult emotionally, the educational, linguistic and personal benefits are substantial, and I believe they outweigh the drawbacks.

prompts.prompt:
Some companies are introducing a four-day working week, in which employees work for four days instead of five but receive the same salary.

Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
The idea of a four-day working week has attracted growing interest, with several companies reporting positive results from trials. In my view, the advantages of this change outweigh the disadvantages, although it would not suit every type of business.

The main benefit is a better balance between work and private life. With three days off, employees have more time to spend with their families, exercise and pursue hobbies, which reduces stress and improves their health. Companies that tried the system found that workers took fewer sick days and were more concentrated while at work, so productivity often remained the same or even increased. A shorter week can also help organisations to recruit and keep talented staff, since many people value free time as much as money. In addition, fewer commuting days means less traffic and pollution.

However, the system has drawbacks. Some jobs, such as nursing, teaching and customer service, cannot simply be compressed into four days, because people still need these services five or seven days a week. Employers might have to hire additional staff or pay overtime, which would increase costs. In other cases, employees may be forced to do the same amount of work in fewer hours, leading to exhaustion rather than relaxation. Finally, businesses that deal with companies working a five-day week may find communication more difficult.

These problems, though, can be managed through careful planning, such as rotating days off so that services remain available. Where jobs involve mainly office work, the evidence suggests that people can complete their tasks more efficiently when they know that they have a long weekend ahead.

In conclusion, despite practical difficulties in some sectors, a four-day week can make employees happier and healthier without damaging productivity, so I believe it is a positive development.

prompts.prompt:
Many cities are banning private cars from their centres and encouraging people to use public transport, bicycles or walking instead.

Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Traffic congestion and pollution have become serious problems in cities around the world, and a growing number of local governments have responded by banning private vehicles from central areas. I believe that the advantages of this policy are greater than the disadvantages, provided that good alternatives are available.

The most obvious advantage is cleaner air. Exhaust fumes from cars are a major cause of breathing problems, and removing them can improve public health, especially for children and the elderly. Noise is reduced as well, which makes the centre a more pleasant place to live and work. Streets that were once full of traffic can be turned into pedestrian areas with cafés and markets, attracting tourists and increasing local trade. In addition, fewer vehicles mean fewer accidents, so streets become safer for cyclists and pedestrians.

Nevertheless, there are disadvantages. Some shop owners fear that customers who cannot park nearby will go elsewhere, and delivery companies may find it difficult to supply their goods. People with disabilities or those who are elderly may depend on cars to move around, and a ban could make their lives harder. Moreover, if public transport is slow, crowded or expensive, residents may feel that they have been forced to accept a worse service.

These difficulties can be addressed with sensible exceptions, such as permits for deliveries and special parking for disabled drivers, together with investment in buses, trams and metros. Several European cities that have taken these steps have seen business improve rather than decline.

In conclusion, car-free city centres bring significant benefits for health, safety and quality of life, and with careful planning, their drawbacks can be minimised, so I believe the policy is worthwhile.

prompts.prompt:
Plastic waste is polluting rivers, oceans and land in many parts of the world.

What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Plastic pollution has become one of the most visible environmental problems of our time, with bottles and bags found everywhere from city streets to the deepest oceans. This essay will outline the main problems this causes and suggest practical solutions.

The first problem is the harm to wildlife. Marine animals such as turtles and seabirds often mistake plastic for food and die as a result, while fishing nets abandoned at sea trap and kill many creatures. A second problem is that plastic breaks into tiny pieces called microplastics, which enter the food chain and, eventually, human bodies. The long-term effects on health are not yet fully understood, which is a cause for concern. Finally, plastic does not rot for hundreds of years, so waste dumped today will remain for generations and make land and water unattractive and unhealthy.

There are several ways to tackle these issues. Governments should take the lead by banning unnecessary single-use items, such as plastic straws and bags, and by taxing producers of heavy packaging. Some countries have introduced deposit schemes, in which customers pay a small amount for a bottle and are refunded when they return it, which has raised recycling rates dramatically. Companies, too, have a responsibility to develop alternatives, such as paper or biodegradable materials, and to design products that are easier to recycle.

Individuals can also make a difference. Carrying a reusable water bottle and shopping bag, avoiding heavily packaged goods and joining beach clean-ups all help reduce waste. Education in schools can encourage these habits from an early age.

In conclusion, plastic pollution harms animals, enters our food and lasts for centuries, but effective laws, better products and responsible personal choices can significantly reduce the problem.

prompts.prompt:
The number of overweight young people is rising rapidly in many countries.

What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
In many countries, doctors are reporting that more children and teenagers are overweight than ever before. This trend is worrying, and it is important to understand both its causes and the measures that could reverse it.

Several factors explain the increase. Firstly, modern diets contain far more processed food, sugary drinks and fast food, which are cheap, heavily advertised and high in calories. Secondly, young people are much less active than in the past. Instead of playing outside, many spend hours in front of screens, and a large number are driven to school rather than walking. Finally, busy parents often have little time to prepare fresh meals, so children grow up accustomed to convenient but unhealthy food.

The consequences are serious. Overweight children are more likely to develop diabetes and heart problems later in life, and they may also suffer from low self-esteem or bullying. In the long term, the cost of treating these illnesses places a heavy burden on health services.

Fortunately, there are practical solutions. Schools should offer healthy lunches, remove vending machines selling sweets and provide at least an hour of physical activity every day. Governments could limit advertising of junk food aimed at children and tax sugary drinks, using the money to fund sports facilities. Parents also have a vital role: they can cook simple meals at home, eat together as a family and set limits on screen time. Community programmes that make exercise enjoyable, such as free football clubs, can motivate young people who dislike traditional gym lessons.

In conclusion, rising obesity among the young is mainly caused by poor diets and inactivity, but a combination of better school policies, government action and family habits can help to solve it.

prompts.prompt:
In many countries, a growing number of elderly people live alone and have little contact with their families.

What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Because of changing lifestyles, it is increasingly common for older people to live by themselves, often far from their children. While some enjoy their independence, many suffer as a result. This essay will examine the main problems and propose some solutions.

The most serious problem is loneliness. An elderly person who spends days without speaking to anyone may become depressed, and studies suggest that isolation can damage physical health as much as smoking. Another problem is safety. Older people who live alone may fall at home and be unable to call for help, or they may have difficulty cooking, shopping and taking their medicines properly. There is also the risk of being targeted by criminals, who sometimes trick lonely people into giving away their savings.

Several measures could improve the situation. Firstly, families should make a greater effort to stay in touch. Regular phone or video calls, and visits whenever possible, can make older relatives feel valued. Secondly, local authorities and charities could organise volunteer schemes in which young people visit elderly neighbours, help with shopping or simply have a chat. Community centres can run lunches, exercise classes and activities that encourage older people to meet others of their age. Thirdly, technology can help: simple alarm devices worn around the neck allow a person to call for help immediately, and tablets with easy-to-use screens allow them to speak to grandchildren abroad.

Finally, governments should invest in home care services so that older people can remain in their own homes safely, rather than being moved into institutions.

In conclusion, loneliness and lack of safety are the main difficulties for elderly people living alone, but family contact, community support and sensible use of technology can greatly improve their quality of life.

prompts.prompt:
In many countries, university graduates find it difficult to get a job that matches their qualifications.

What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Obtaining a degree used to be a reliable way to secure a good job. Nowadays, however, many graduates in a number of countries struggle to find work in their field, and some accept positions that do not require a degree at all. This essay will consider the causes of the situation and some possible remedies.

One cause is that the number of graduates has grown faster than the number of suitable jobs. As more young people attend university, competition for each position becomes more intense, and employers can afford to be selective. Another cause is a mismatch between what universities teach and what employers need. Graduates may have plenty of theoretical knowledge but lack practical skills, such as teamwork, communication and the use of up-to-date technology. In addition, many students choose popular subjects without checking the demand for them, so that some professions are overcrowded while others, like engineering and skilled trades, face shortages.

The consequences include frustration, wasted talent and heavy student debt, which can discourage young people from further study.

To solve the problem, universities should cooperate more closely with businesses, offering internships and projects that give students real experience before they graduate. Courses should be reviewed regularly to ensure that they include the skills that employers value. Governments could provide clear information about the job market, so that students can make informed decisions, and might fund vocational training as an attractive alternative to a university degree. Graduates themselves can improve their chances by learning additional skills, such as a foreign language, and by building professional networks.

In conclusion, an oversupply of graduates and a gap between education and employment are the main causes of graduate unemployment, and closer links between universities, employers and governments could provide effective solutions.

prompts.prompt:
Many people now spend most of their free time on social media.

Why do you think this is happening?
Is it a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Social media platforms have become an everyday habit for millions of people, who often check them dozens of times a day. There are several reasons for this trend, and, on balance, I believe that its effects are more negative than positive.

The main reason is that these platforms are designed to be addictive. Features such as endless scrolling, notifications and "likes" give users small rewards that make them want to return. Social media also meets a basic human need for connection: people can keep in touch with friends and relatives who live far away, share photographs and discover what others are doing. In addition, it is extremely convenient, since a smartphone is always in the pocket and offers entertainment, news and conversation in a single place. For many young people, not being online means being excluded from their social group.

Is this positive? Admittedly, there are some benefits. People can find communities that share their interests, learn new skills from videos and, for small businesses, advertise at low cost. However, I believe the disadvantages are more significant. Time spent scrolling replaces face-to-face conversation, exercise and hobbies, and many users report feeling anxious or inadequate after comparing themselves with the carefully selected images of others' lives. Sleep is also affected when people use their phones late at night. Furthermore, false information can spread quickly, and young users may be exposed to bullying.

Therefore, although social media has useful features, I think it becomes harmful when it takes over most of a person's leisure time. A healthier approach would be to limit use to a fixed period each day and to spend the rest of the time on real-world activities.

In conclusion, social media is popular because it is addictive and convenient, but excessive use is a negative development for well-being.

prompts.prompt:
In many countries, young people are leaving small towns and villages to live in large cities.

Why are they doing this?
What can be done to encourage them to stay in their home areas?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Across the world, small communities are losing their young inhabitants to big cities. Understanding the reasons for this movement is the first step towards finding ways to keep young people at home.

The main reason is economic. Small towns often have limited employment, with few jobs outside farming and local shops, and wages are usually low. Large cities, in contrast, offer a wide variety of careers and the chance of a much higher income. Education is another factor, since universities and specialised colleges are mostly situated in urban areas, and many students never return after graduating. Finally, young people are attracted by the lifestyle of the city, including entertainment, nightlife and the opportunity to meet new people, which can seem more exciting than the quiet routine of a village.

Several measures could persuade more of them to stay. Governments and local authorities should invest in creating jobs outside the big cities, for example by offering tax benefits to companies that open offices or factories in smaller towns. Improved internet connections would allow people to work remotely for employers elsewhere while living in a more affordable and peaceful place. Education is also important: colleges that offer local training courses, such as agriculture, tourism or technology, could help young people to gain qualifications without leaving. Furthermore, towns could improve their facilities by building sports centres, cinemas and cafés, and by supporting festivals and cultural events that make local life more lively.

Finally, affordable housing schemes for young families would make it easier for them to settle down in the community where they grew up.

In conclusion, young people leave small towns mainly for work, education and excitement, and creating local jobs, better connections and a more attractive social life are the most effective ways of encouraging them to stay.

prompts.prompt:
In many countries, fewer young people take part in regular sports and physical exercise than in the past.

What are the reasons for this?
What can schools do to encourage young people to be more active?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
Doctors and teachers are increasingly concerned that young people today exercise much less than previous generations. There are several explanations, and schools are in a strong position to change this.

One reason is the popularity of digital entertainment. Video games, streaming services and social media can occupy hours of a teenager's day, and these activities are performed sitting down. Another reason is that many children no longer play outdoors, because parents worry about traffic and safety, so they are driven everywhere rather than walking or cycling. Academic pressure also plays a role: students who face heavy homework and exams may feel that they have no time for sport. In addition, some young people lose interest because competitive school sports focus on the best players, leaving others feeling embarrassed or left out.

Schools can do a great deal to improve the situation. First, they should make physical education a priority in the timetable, with daily sessions rather than one lesson per week. Second, they could offer a wider variety of activities, such as dance, climbing, yoga and cycling, so that every student can find something enjoyable, not only football or athletics. Emphasis should be placed on participation and fun instead of winning, which would encourage less confident pupils. Third, schools can organise inter-class competitions and active breaks during lessons, and give awards for effort. They should also explain to students and parents how exercise improves concentration and mood, which is beneficial for academic results as well.

Finally, cooperation with local clubs would give students opportunities to continue activities after school.

In conclusion, screens, safety concerns, academic pressure and unattractive sports lessons explain the decline in activity, but schools can reverse it by offering more varied and enjoyable physical education.

prompts.prompt:
Families in many countries are now much smaller than they were fifty years ago, and many couples choose to have only one child or none.

Why is this happening?
Is it a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
prompts.modelAnswer:
The average family has become noticeably smaller in recent decades, particularly in cities. This essay will explain the reasons for this trend and consider whether it should be welcomed.

There are several explanations. First, the cost of raising a child has risen dramatically. Housing, education and healthcare are expensive, and many couples feel that they cannot afford more than one child. Second, more women are now in education and employment, and they often delay having children until their thirties to build a career, which naturally limits the size of their families. Third, advances in medicine mean that more children survive into adulthood, so parents no longer need to have many children to ensure that some will live. Finally, attitudes have changed, as it is now more acceptable to choose a life without children or to have a small family so that more time and money can be devoted to each child.

In my view, the trend has both benefits and drawbacks, but the drawbacks may be more serious in the long run. On the positive side, smaller families put less pressure on housing, natural resources and the environment, and parents can give each child more attention. However, if birth rates remain low for many years, the population grows old, and there are fewer young workers to pay taxes and care for the elderly, which could threaten pensions and health services. Children without siblings may also miss the experience of learning to share and cooperate.

Governments can reduce these risks by providing affordable childcare and flexible working conditions so that having children becomes more practical.

In conclusion, smaller families result from financial pressure, careers and changing values, and although they bring some advantages, I consider the ageing of society to be a serious concern.
